questions.question: What is wrong with this commit message: 'feat: Added login page.'?
choices: It uses past tense ('Added') and ends with a period
questions.explanation: Two violations: 'Added' is past tense (should be 'add' in imperative mood), and the description ends with a period (not allowed). Correct: 'feat: add login page'

questions.question: Why does Conventional Commits require imperative mood instead of past tense?
choices: It's just a stylistic preference with no functional difference
Because commit messages describe what the commit WILL do, not what was done
Because Git only understands imperative commands
Because past tense messages are too long
questions.explanation: Imperative mood ('add login') reads as 'this commit will add login page', which is a forward-looking description of the change. Past tense ('added') is grammatically awkward when applied to future code that will use this commit.

questions.question: Which of these is a valid Conventional Commit type?
questions.explanation: Only a fixed set of types are valid: feat, fix, chore, docs, style, refactor, test, perf, ci, build. 'updated', 'changed', and 'modified' are not in the list.
